---

Group and dock UI elements to the edges of the viewport to maximize visible screen real estate.

A. Top Information Bar (Docked Top):
- Combine \"Location Name\" (Left), \"Aether Shards / Day Count\" (Center), and \"Rift Activity Level\" (Right) into a single, sleek semi-transparent glassmorphism top header (height: ~40px).

B. Target @COMMENT_BODY@ Status Frames:
- Player Frame (Bottom-Left): Stack Player Portrait, Health Bar (green), Aether Energy Bar (blue), and Class Icon.
- Companion Frames (Left Sidebar): Compact, vertical unit frames showing the 3 active monsters' HP bars, elemental icons, and Sync Rate percentage.
- Target Frame (Top-Center / Above Entity): Anchor enemy health bars and status effect icons directly above enemy sprites in the world space, floating naturally with their movement.

C. Action Hotbar @COMMENT_BODY@ Controls (Bottom-Center):
- Clean Action Grid: Merge keybinds into a unified bottom hotbar:
  [WASD - Move] | [Space - Primary Attack] | [Q - Class Ability] | [E - Snare] | [1-3 - Squad Commands]
- Virtual Overlay (Touch/Mobile Only): Automatically hide onscreen D-Pads and touch buttons when keyboard/mouse input is detected.

D. Color Palette @COMMENT_BODY@ Typography:
- Palette: Dark Slate (#0F172A) frame background, Aether Cyan (#06B6D4) primary highlights, Flame (#F97316), Hydro (#3B82F6), Gale (#10B981), Terra (#EAB308).
- Font: Use a crisp, highly legible pixel font (e.g., 'Press Start 2P' for headers, 'Silkscreen' or clean sans-serif for numbers/tooltips).

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

- Overhaul Aetherbound’s existing playable game with crisp pixel-art rendering and a streamlined, modular HUD.

## Requirements
- Pixel-art characters, monsters, detailed environment, lighting, particles, floating combat text, and responsive edge-docked UI.
- Include player and companion status, enemy health/status, action hotbar and controls; hide touch controls after keyboard/mouse input.
- Keep the game playable; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Save a small JPEG screenshot for a visual check and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Applied the overhaul directly to the existing single-file game in `index.html`.
- Used CSS pixel sprites drawn on the canvas rather than introducing external sprite assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked styling for a dark slate/cyan pixel-font HUD, responsive layouts, player and companion frames, hotbar, and mobile controls.
- Replaced canvas actors and environment with pixel-grid sprites, textured ground, canopy light shafts, a crystal glow, shadows, and square particle/combat effects.
- Added player Aether energy display and regeneration; class ability now costs 18 energy.
- Hid mobile overlays on keyboard input or mouse pointer input.

### Active
- Validate the game in a browser, fix any issues, and capture/inspect the requested JPEG screenshot.
- Check `index.html` for syntax/runtime issues and polish any UI/rendering defects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the edited `index.html`, especially the canvas enemy-tag positioning and the dynamically generated companion frames.
2. Run the game and verify movement, combat, ability energy, capture, and mobile controls.
3. Save a JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect the latest image.
4. Report assumptions and verification results to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Existing game and all current UI, CSS, canvas, and gameplay changes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Canvas rendering looks up `$('enemy-tag')`, but the existing enemy tag markup uses `class="enemy-tag"` without that ID; dynamic positioning may therefore not work.

  go-forward                  go forward to the next page

  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:

  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key

## Objective
- Overhaul Aetherbound with crisp pixel-art rendering and a streamlined, modular HUD.
- Verify desktop and mobile layouts and gameplay in a browser, then capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Pixel-art characters, monsters, environment, lighting, particles, and floating combat text.
- Responsive edge-docked UI for player, companion, enemy, actions, and controls; hide touch controls after keyboard/mouse input.
- Keep gameplay playable and make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Applied the overhaul directly in `index.html`, using CSS pixel sprites drawn on canvas instead of adding external sprite assets.
- Added Aether energy regeneration; the class ability costs 18 energy.
- Fixed enemy-tag lookup to query `.enemy-tag` rather than the nonexistent `enemy-tag` ID.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked the HUD and canvas visuals with a pixel-art theme, party/player status, hotbar, environment, effects, and mobile controls.
- Fixed the CSS cascade: a missing closing brace in `.scene-vignette` caused the subsequent overhaul styles to be ignored.
- Verified corrected desktop layout at 1280×800: sidebar is absolutely positioned, player card is edge-docked, and rightbar is hidden.
- Passed JavaScript syntax validation with `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Opened the game in Chromium; page renders and browser snapshot shows the game UI.

### Active
- Verify mobile layout and touch controls, then exercise movement, combat, ability energy, capture, and input-mode control visibility.
- Recapture and inspect the JPEG after the CSS fix; the existing `/tmp/opencode/aetherbound-desktop.jpg` predates the correction.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Resize the browser to mobile dimensions and verify HUD, touch controls, and keyboard/mouse control visibility.
2. Exercise movement, combat, ability energy use, and capture in the browser.
3. Capture and inspect an updated 1280×800 JPEG; check browser console for any remaining errors.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game markup, styles, canvas rendering, controls, and gameplay logic.
- `/tmp/opencode/aetherbound-desktop.jpg`: Existing screenshot, captured before the cascade fix and needing replacement.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The CSS fix closes the `.scene-vignette` declaration before `.scene-top`; browser now loads the full stylesheet (216 rules).
- Prior browser console error was only `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://127.0.0.1:4173/favicon.ico:0`.
